To test this hypothesis, we avoid the confounding complexity of natural language benchmarks, where syntax, semantics, and rote memorization are inextricably entangled. Instead, we seek the minimal universality class of logical inference. We focus on two tasks that isolate the physics of reasoning: the symmetric group S 3 S_{3} (the mathematical atom of non-Abelian logic) and high-complexity variable binding on S 10 S_{10} (a proxy for the symbolic state-tracking required for coherent reasoning in LLMs) [ 19 , 20 ] . We argue that the failure modes observed in these minimal systems represent the lower bound of fragility for large-scale models. If an architecture cannot maintain topological protection in the simplest non-commutative group ( S 3 S_{3} ), it cannot be expected to maintain causal consistency in the complex non-Abelian structure of natural language. Thus, just as the 2D Ising model isolates the physics of phase transitions without modeling the complexity of real alloys, our tasks isolate the topology of reasoning without the noise of syntax, a methodological approach shared with recent studies on algorithmic generalization [ 21 ] . We identify this topological framework with an effective topological quantum field theory (TQFT). We emphasize that this is an effective description of the macroscopic information dynamics [ 22 ] , not a claim that the neural network operates on quantum mechanical principles.
